metadata.title: Why a Cooled Electron Never Stops
metadata.key_case: Cool a trapped electron toward absolute zero — it still jitters. Why won't it stop?
deferred: a proof of the uncertainty bound

beats.narration_text: Cool this trapped electron toward absolute zero. Everything else stops moving. It doesn't.
beats.visual_intent: an electron in a box; a thermometer falls to ~0 K; the particle keeps shaking

beats.narration_text: Squeeze the box narrower and the slowest wiggle it can hold gets faster — not slower.
beats.visual_intent: well width L animates smaller; the lowest standing wave speeds up

beats.narration_text: Widen it and that same lowest wiggle calms down — but it never flattens to a straight line.
beats.visual_intent: L animates wider; amplitude drops but never reaches zero

beats.narration_text: Watch why: pin both ends to the walls and you are forced to bend the wave, and bending costs motion.
beats.visual_intent: the same wave morphing as the walls move; endpoints stay pinned at zero

beats.narration_text: So the smallest allowed energy is set by how tightly you confine it: E-one goes as one over L-squared.
beats.visual_intent: the expression E₁ = π²ħ² / (2mL²) lands next to the pinned wave

beats.narration_text: Read the symbols: L is the box width, m the mass. Smaller box, higher floor. That is the whole claim.
beats.visual_intent: each symbol labeled in plain words; the 1/L² term highlighted

beats.narration_text: That is why the cooled electron never rests: stopping would pin it to one spot, and confinement forbids it.
beats.visual_intent: return to the opening electron, now labeled with its non-zero ground energy

beats.narration_text: We did not build the higher rungs or prove the bound — that is the next video. Your turn.
beats.visual_intent: outro card; the exercise shown on screen
beats.viewer_exercise: Compute E₁ for L = 1 nm and L = 2 nm and confirm the energy quadruples when L halves.
